summary.en: Build the prefix function, reuse matched borders after a mismatch, and find patterns without moving the text index backwards.
summary.bn: prefix function বানাও, অমিলে আগের border কাজে লাগাও, আর টেক্সটের ইনডেক্স পেছনে না নিয়েই ম্যাচ খোঁজো।

notes: The demonstrated programs use C17; the lesson states their input and arithmetic bounds.

sections.title: Keep useful information after a mismatch
Follow a chain of shorter borders
Why the fallback skips no candidate
Lengths are not indices of the same kind

examples.title: Build the prefix table
examples.explanationHtml: Input ababaca produces 0 0 1 2 3 0 1. This is the algorithm animated by the prefix lab. Try aaaa to see every new character extend the border.

examples.title: Search using matched length
examples.explanationHtml: The full matcher reports positions zero and two for ababa and aba. After every complete match it falls back to pi[m-1], so overlapping occurrences survive. A pattern longer than the text simply never reaches matched length m.

examples.title: List every border length
examples.explanationHtml: For ababab, following pi links gives lengths four and two. The program prints them longest first. It excludes the whole word because borders here are proper and excludes zero because the display lists nonempty borders.

practice.title: Compute pi for ababaca and explain the fallback at c.
practice.statementHtml: Compute pi for ababaca and explain the fallback at c.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: The array is [0,0,1,2,3,0,1]. At index 5, c fails against pattern[3]=b. Follow pi[2]=1, fail against pattern[1]=b, then reach zero and fail against a. Thus pi[5]=0.

practice.title: Why does matching aba inside ababa set j to one after its first match?
practice.statementHtml: Why does matching aba inside ababa set j to one after its first match?
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: The matched aba has border a of length one. That final a can begin the next overlapping occurrence. pi[2]=1 retains it, so the next b and a complete the match at start two.

quiz.prompt: Which value is pi[0] for every nonempty pattern?
quiz.explanation: A single character has no nonempty proper prefix that is also a suffix.

quiz.prompt: What does proper exclude in the KMP border definition?
quiz.explanation: A proper prefix is shorter than the complete prefix under consideration.

quiz.prompt: For pattern aaaa, what is pi[3]?
quiz.explanation: The longest proper border of aaaa is aaa, of length three.

quiz.prompt: Which fallback preserves the longest remaining candidate after a mismatch at matched length j?
quiz.explanation: The next candidate is a proper border of the prefix of length j.

quiz.prompt: What happens to the text index during KMP fallback?
options: It stays on the same text byte
quiz.explanation: Only the matched prefix length changes until that text byte is resolved.

quiz.prompt: Why reset j to pi[m-1] after reporting a match?
quiz.explanation: A proper suffix of the completed pattern may already match the next occurrence prefix.

quiz.prompt: What makes KMP linear despite its nested while loop?
options: Fallbacks consume previously gained prefix length
quiz.explanation: The matched length increases at most once per outer character, bounding total decreases too.

quiz.prompt: For aaaa, what prefix length is stored at its final index?
quiz.explanation: Every new a extends the preceding border by one, giving three.

quiz.prompt: Which matched length remains when aba completes in KMP?
quiz.explanation: pi[2] retains the trailing a as a one-character border.

quiz.prompt: Which two border lengths does the chain for ababab visit?
quiz.explanation: The longest border abab has length four, whose own border ab has length two.

examQuestions.question: State the invariant and justify the time and space costs of KMP Algorithm.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Suppose the current candidate prefix of length j already matches a suffix of the processed prefix. If the new character fails to extend it, any shorter successful candidate must itself be a border of that length-j string. Otherwise its earlier characters would not agree with the suffix already known to match.

The longest such candidate has length pi[j-1]. Following that link therefore skips only lengths that cannot be valid borders. Repeating the argument visits all remaining possible border lengths from longest to shortest. The first extension found is the longest; if none exists, zero is correct.

During text matching, the invariant says that pattern[0..j) equals the suffix of the consumed text of length j, and no longer candidate survives. A successful character comparison extends it. A failure follows the same exhaustive border chain, preserving possible alignments without decreasing i.

When j reaches m, the last m text bytes equal the pattern, so the reported position is a real match. Any future overlapping match must begin with a proper border of this completed pattern. Retaining its longest border and following further fallbacks preserves all such possibilities. Every occurrence is consequently reported.

The prefix-building outer loop advances i at most m-1 times. A successful extension increases j by one, so there are at most m-1 such increases. Every fallback strictly decreases j. Across the entire loop, these decreases cannot exceed the amount previously accumulated through increases.

This amortised argument bounds total fallback iterations by O(m), even though a single position may follow several links. Construction therefore takes O(m) time and O(m) space for pi. It is incorrect to multiply every outer step by m merely because a while loop is nested inside it.

The same reasoning applies to matching: consuming a text character advances i, while positive matched length can only be decreased after it was increased. Total matching work is O(n). Reporting z occurrences adds O(z), already at most O(n) for a nonempty pattern. Combined time is O(n+m), with O(m) auxiliary table space.

The bounded examples reserve twenty-four table entries regardless of shorter input. General asymptotic space describes a table sized to m, not the small fixed capacity selected for an educational program. Neither program stores a copy of every matched substring.
